result.title: One Monitor Does Not Fit All: Formalism-Agnostic Runtime Verification for Agentic AI
result.summary: Agentic AI systems combine model decisions, mutable state, tool calls, and delegation to external agents. Monitoring them requires observations from different execution boundaries, while prevention requires control before an operation produces its effect. We present AgenticRV, a runtime-verification architecture that separates these boundaries from the monitoring formalism. Adapters emit canonical events; each monitor receives its own projection and abstraction; and a decision policy uses normalised verdicts to select a reaction supported by the responsible adapter. We formalise when observations suffice, monitor replacement preserves decisions, and blocking prevents unsafe effects. We also distinguish rejected attempts from completed effects, avoiding the assumption that a blocked request must leave every monitor in a permanent violation state. The Python implementation supports LangGraph, MCP, and A2A. A controlled LangGraph experiment combines an external Reelay temporal monitor with a programmatic report monitor; ablations show why both are needed for the selected requirements. Differential checks and cross-adapter tests provide further integration evidence. An LLM-driven incident-response example illustrates the same enforcement path, while existing microbenchmarks isolate framework costs. The results support reuse of monitoring methods at explicit control boundaries, subject to the stated observation and deployment assumptions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AgenticRV 运行时验证架构，把监控形式与执行边界解耦：适配器发出规范事件，各 monitor 接收自己的投影与抽象，决策策略依据规范化裁决选择由相应适配器支持的反应；并形式化观察充分性、monitor 替换保持决策、阻断阻止不安全效果等条件，附 LangGraph/MCP/A2A 实现与实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按控制边界投影观察」与「区分被拒尝试和已完成效果」的形式化，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的运行时监测、裁决归一化及 STOP/提交决策提供可核查的线索，属较远领域的具体启发。
